<translate>
<!--T:1-->
A catalogue raisonné is a web of links: an artwork is a study for another, was owned by a collector, was shown in an exhibition and illustrated in a book. openCR records each of these links once, in a defined place, and shows it from both sides.

<!--T:2-->
This page lists every kind of link. There are two families:
* '''links between records of the same kind''', for example artwork to artwork;
* '''links between different kinds of records''', for example artwork to publication.

<!--T:3-->
For the building blocks themselves, see [[How openCR is structured]].

<!--T:4-->
== Two rules for all links ==
'''Enter each link once.''' A link between two records is stored once, and openCR shows it from both sides. Where a link has a direction, the other side shows the reverse wording automatically: if a drawing ''is preparatory study for'' a painting, the painting shows the reverse wording, ''has preparatory study''. Entering the reverse link as well makes it appear twice.

<!--T:5-->
'''Mind the direction.''' "A ''is preparatory study for'' B" means that A is the study. Entered the wrong way round, every displayed phrase is reversed. For symmetric links, such as ''is similar to'', the direction does not matter, but they are still entered only once.

<!--T:6-->
== Links between artworks ==
Artworks have the richest set of links among themselves. Each kind has its own place, and they are not interchangeable.

<!--T:7-->
{| class="wikitable"
! Kind of link !! Where !! Use it for
|-
| '''Parts''' || ''Parts of the object'' section || One work made of several pieces, such as a triptych or an assembly
|-
| '''Suite''' || ''Group (suite)'' in the main data: ''Head of a group'' on the suite; ''Member of a group'', with the ''Head of the group'' and the ''Position'', on each member. ''Kind of group'' (suite, folder, installation, group, book or series) is set on the head and on each member. || Separately catalogued works forming a series, such as a portfolio of prints
|-
| '''Print editions''' || ''Editions'' section || The impressions of a print: regular edition, artist's proofs, trial proofs and so on
|-
| '''Copies''' || ''Copies'' section || The casts or copies of a sculpture or multiple
|-
| '''Catalogue relations''' || ''Related objects'' || Art-historical links: study, version, copy, model and so on
|-
| '''Correction and supplementary records''' || Set by the platform administrator; shown below the main record || Additional records that correct or supplement a main record
|}

<!--T:8-->
=== Parts or suite? ===
{| class="wikitable"
! Question !! Then use
|-
| Is it one work in several pieces, sharing one title and one date? || '''Parts'''
|-
| Are they separate works, each with its own title and date, that form a series? || '''Suite'''
|}

<!--T:9-->
=== Catalogue relations ===
The ''Related objects'' section offers these links. The pop-up shows each pair with both wordings, and ''Reading'' spells out the sentence with the titles of the two works, so a link can be entered on either of them: on the drawing, pick the painting and choose the reading in which the drawing is the study; or on the painting, pick the drawing and choose the reading in which the painting has the study. Either way, enter it only once; the other work shows the reverse wording automatically, and the pop-up refuses the same link a second time. Only works of the same artist can be linked.
{| class="wikitable"
! Link !! Shown on the other work as
|-
| is preparatory study for || has preparatory study
|-
| is study after || has study
|-
| is rendering of || has rendering
|-
| is model for || has model
|-
| is plan of || has plan
|-
| is cartoon for || has cartoon
|-
| is printing surface for || is printed from printing surface
|-
| is version of || has version
|-
| is copy after || has copy
|-
| is replica of || has replica
|-
| is facsimile of || has facsimile
|-
| is derived from || is source for
|-
| is based on preparatory work || is preparatory for
|-
| is based on || is base of
|-
| is reworking of || was reworked as
|-
| is part of || has part
|-
| was formerly part of || had formerly part
|-
| has context || is context for
|-
| depicts || is depicted in
|-
| is similar to || is similar to
|-
| is pendant of || is pendant of
|-
| is related to || is related to
|}

<!--T:10-->
A study for a painting is a catalogue relation, not a member of a suite. Plate 3 of a portfolio of twelve is a member of a suite, not a catalogue relation.

<!--T:11-->
=== Entries for a single part or edition ===
Many sections of an artwork can refer either to the whole work or to one of its parts, print editions or copies. Each part, each edition and each entry of ''Copies'' has its own sub-sections, with their own plus icon: add an entry there to narrow it down, or in the work's own section when it applies to the whole work. An entry cannot be moved to another part or edition later.

<!--T:12-->
{| class="wikitable"
! Section !! Part !! Print edition !! Copies
|-
| Materials & Techniques || ✓ || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Attributes || ✓ || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Dimensions || ✓ || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Agents || ✓ || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Dates || – || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Notes || – || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Individual copies || ✓ || ✓ || ✓
|-
| Images, Provenance, Transactions, References || – || – || –
|}

<!--T:13-->
Images (apart from those of an individual copy), ownership, sales and literature always refer to the work as a whole. Create parts and editions '''before''' the entries that refer to them.

<!--T:14-->
== Links between publications ==
''Related Publications'' links a publication to another one: is part of, is a version of, is copy of, facsimile of, is based on, is preparatory for, derived from, is similar to, is related to. The same rules apply: one entry per link, the reverse wording is shown automatically, and the same link is refused a second time. See [[Publications#Events, languages and related publications|Publications]].

<!--T:15-->
== Links between directory entries ==
''Related persons and organizations'' links people and institutions to each other: works for, is member of, is colleague of, is founder of, is funder of, is owner of, is sponsor of, is teacher of / is student of, is child of, is sibling of, is related (family, emotional or abstract), is successor of / is predecessor of, has taken over, has absorbed, has met, knows. A relation can carry the period during which it existed, and the pop-up refuses the same relation with the same dates a second time, from either side. See [[Directory#Sections|Directory]].

<!--T:16-->
== Artists and events ==
Artists are not linked to other artists directly, and events not to other events. Artists meet in shared records instead: a group exhibition lists all its participating artists, a publication all the artists it is about.

<!--T:17-->
== Links between different kinds of records ==
The table lists, for each kind of record, the links it holds to other kinds and the section in which they are entered.

<!--T:18-->
=== From an artwork ===
{| class="wikitable"
! To !! Section !! Meaning
|-
| Artist || (set when the work is created; cannot be changed) || The catalogue the work belongs to
|-
| [[Directory]] || ''Agents'' || Printer, publisher, foundry, photographer, co-author and other people involved
|-
| Directory || ''Provenance'' || The owners
|-
| Directory || ''Transactions'' || Seller, buyer and intermediary of a sale
|-
| Directory || ''Dates'' || Who performed a dated action, such as a restoration
|-
| Directory || ''Attributes'' || A person or institution named in a mark, such as a dedication
|-
| Directory || Images || The photographer of a photograph
|-
| [[Publications]] || ''References'' || The literature that mentions or illustrates the work
|-
| Directory || ''References'' || A person or institution that records the work, for example in an inventory
|-
| Directory || ''Editions'', ''Copies'' || Who authorised a posthumous edition, and who received an edition
|-
| Directory || ''Individual copies'' || The holder of a single copy
|-
| Publications or directory || ''Other Titles'' || The publication that uses a further title, or the person who gave it
|-
| [[Events]] || ''Exhibitions'' || The exhibitions where the work was shown, with the lender (a directory entry)
|-
| Events || ''Transactions'' || The auction or fair at which a sale took place
|-
| Tags || ''Tags'' || The artist's keywords and the general tags that apply to the work
|}

<!--T:19-->
=== From a publication ===
{| class="wikitable"
! To !! Section !! Meaning
|-
| [[Artists]] || ''Related artists'' || The artists the publication is about; this is what puts it into their bibliography
|-
| Artists || ''References to artists'' || The pages per artist
|-
| [[Directory]] || ''Agents'' || Authors, editors, publishers and other contributors
|-
| [[Events]] || ''Related events'' || The events the publication documents
|-
| [[Objects|Artworks]] || ''Referenced Objects'' || The artworks it mentions or illustrates (the same link as the artwork's ''References'')
|}

<!--T:20-->
=== From an event ===
{| class="wikitable"
! To !! Section !! Meaning
|-
| [[Artists]] || ''Related artists'' || The participating artists and their relation to the event
|-
| [[Directory]] || ''Related agents'' || Organisers, curators, galleries, sponsors and others
|-
| [[Objects|Artworks]] || ''Related objects'' || The works shown (the same link as the artwork's ''Exhibitions'')
|-
| [[Publications]] || ''Related publications'' || Publications about the event (the same link as the publication's ''Related events'')
|}

<!--T:21-->
=== From an artist ===
{| class="wikitable"
! To !! Section !! Meaning
|-
| [[Directory]] || ''Artist - Relations with the directory'' || Gallerist, publisher, collector, mentor, family, heir and others
|-
| Directory || (no section; shown on the directory entry as ''Collection of objects'') || Institutions holding works by the artist
|-
| Directory || ''Collecting society'' (main data) || The society managing the artist's rights
|-
| Directory || ''Own address-book entry'' (main data) || The person in the directory who is the artist
|-
| [[Publications]] || ''Publications used as reference'' || The pages where publications discuss the artist (the same link as the publication's ''References to artists'')
|}

<!--T:22-->
=== From a directory entry ===
{| class="wikitable"
! To !! Section !! Meaning
|-
| Directory || ''Related persons and organizations'' || Other people and institutions (see [[#Links between directory entries|above]])
|-
| [[Events]] || ''Related events'' || The events in which the entry took part, with its role (the same link as the event's ''Related agents'')
|-
| [[Artists]] || (catalogue link) || Lets the editors of those artists edit the entry, and see and use it even while it is not public; set with ''Easy directory creation'' or on the page ''Address Book''. Not a relationship.
|}
The directory entry's page also lists the links other records hold to it: the artists' relations (''Relations with Artist''), its publications, its collection, the works it owns or owned, the works in which it was an agent, and the works whose marks name it.

<!--T:23-->
=== Dealers and offers ===
A dealer is linked to a directory entry and to the artists they are cleared for; an offer points to an artist and to the work offered. See [[Dealers and offers]].

<!--T:24-->
== Common pitfalls ==
* '''Mirror links.''' Each link is entered once; the other side is shown automatically.
* '''Wrong direction.''' Check which record is the study, the copy or the model before choosing the link.
* '''Suites and relations mixed up.''' Series membership goes into ''Group (suite)'' in the main data, art-historical links into ''Related objects''.
* '''Relationship versus catalogue link.''' To connect a gallery with an artist, use the artist's ''Artist - Relations with the directory''; linking the entry to the artist's catalogue is not a relationship.
* '''The artist as a directory entry.''' When the artist themselves owned a work or performed an action, choose the artist in that entry (''The artist (“by the author”)'' or ''Artist's own collection'') instead of linking a directory entry.
